source.author: verg
source.text: Sunt geminae Somni portae, quarum altera fertur cornea, qua veris facilis datur exitus umbris; altera candenti perfecta nitens elephanto, sed falsa ad caelum mittunt insomnia Manes.
source.text_original: Sunt geminae Somni portae, quarum altera fertur / cornea, qua veris facilis datur exitus umbris; / altera candenti perfecta nitens elephanto, / sed falsa ad caelum mittunt insomnia Manes.
source.text_english: There are twin gates of Sleep, one of which is said to be of horn, through which an easy exit is given to true shades; the other, finished in shining white ivory, but through it the Spirits send false dreams up to heaven.

reuse.text_original: hic geminae aeternum portae, quarum altera dura / semper lege patens populos regesque receptat; / ast aliam temptare nefas et tendere contra: /
reuse.text_english: here are the twin gates, of which one, ever open by a harsh law, receives peoples and kings alike; but to try the other is impious, and to advance against it is forbidden:
